STAGE: orientation
GOAL: Ground the new mechanism in the actual repo rather than in a paper description.
READ: listed the agent working directory.
OBSERVED: <pending>
OPEN: which files define the Stage-2 RQ-VAE training, the probe, and the behaviour graph.

FINAL ANSWER: HYP-GRAPHBOTTLENECK-RQ (one idea, in scope).
What it is: inside the Stage-2 forward pass, between encoder and RQ quantizer, each encoder output is mapped into a fixed-curvature (c=1) Poincare ball, replaced by the equal-weight tangent-space (Frechet) mean of itself and its K training-transition neighbours N(i), and mapped back; that smoothed vector, not the raw encoder output, is what the residual quantizer and reconstruction loss see. Codebook, residual stack, loss and decoder are untouched; there is no extra hyperbolic loss term.
Behaviour: d_beh(i,j) = -log((n_ij+1)/(sqrt(pop_i*pop_j)+1)) counted on training-split adjacent pairs only; N(i) = K smallest-d_beh successors+predecessors, K = ceil(median training out-degree) measured once.
Coupling equation: z' = (1/s) log_0( exp_{p}( (1/(|N|+1)) sum_j log_{p}( exp_0(s z_j) ) ) ), p = exp_0(s z). Behaviour = the set N(i) from d_beh; curvature = the Poincare log/exp triple. Behaviour-off: N empty -> z'=z (identity). Geometry-off: Euclidean mean, same N. Both-on: full run.
Why different from dead rounds: not a codebook Frechet update, not radial/behaviour-ranked assignment, not prefix-transition curvature control, not a metric on finished fixed codes. It changes the tensor the Stage-2 objective differentiates, so gradients reach the encoder through the geometry.
Cost: 72,000 steps unchanged (24 x 3000, four cards); ~1.1M exp/log evaluations and 1.1M float gathers per step at batch 1024, K~16, d=64 => ~10 MFLOP, under 1% of an encoder step, wall clock +3-8%.
Observables: probe Spearman(code dist, d_beh) baseline 0.0402 -> measured after; top-10 behaviour-neighbour overlap baseline 0.0124 -> measured after; level-1 prefix transition entropy (drop expected); per-level MSE (2/3 must stay near baseline); Stage-3 test_recall@10 vs 0.065 with the caveat that one run carries ~0.013 noise.
Main risk: over-smoothing/code collapse (mitigated by self term + unchanged reconstruction loss + MSE logging). Escape route: encoder arranging neighbours symmetrically so the tangent mean cancels (visible as low ||m|| with high MSE).
Safeguards: s from q99 of encoder norms at epoch 0 with 0.8 ball margin, clip, eps floors on norms and Mobius denominators, artanh clip 1-1e-5, empty-N identity, per-epoch ball-radius and MSE checks. No tunable scalar enters the loss.

STEP 1 - design-space scan and de-duplication
GOAL: pick one coupling position not covered by earlier rounds (CURVCTRL-SID per-level curvature from prefix-transition score; BRad-RQ radial assignment from context entropy; poincare-frechet-successor-codebook successor-weighted Frechet codebook updates; BRANCHCURV-MOEB-RQ; TSG-SID; LORENTZ-SUCCPROFILE-SMOOTH-RQ; behcone-prefix-rq; succboost-geoshift; BFRQ-KARCHER-MASS; MIXCURV-FIBRE-RQ; SUCC-GEO-CBTAB) and not a relabelling or a metric swap on fixed code vectors.
READ: the round objective chain (behaviour graph -> tree distance structure -> behaviour embedding -> Gromov delta -> curvature -> hyperbolic RQ-VAE -> SID), the probe definition d_beh = -log((n_ij+1)/(sqrt(pop_i pop_j)+1)) over training transitions only, and the Euclidean RQ-VAE baseline probe numbers 0.0402 Spearman / 0.0124 top-10 behaviour-neighbour overlap.
OBSERVED: every rejected mechanism either (a) moved the metric on frozen codes, or (b) derived curvature from a prefix/transition statistic. None derived the curvature from a geometric property of the behaviour metric itself, and none used a tree (ultrametric) target for the quantized code embedding.
REASONING: the differentiator must be a change to what Stage-2 optimises, with curvature *measured* off the behaviour graph (four-point Gromov delta) and a tree-metric target (MST path-max, i.e. the subdominant ultrametric) imposed by a curved stress on the quantized code embedding, at every prefix depth.
OPEN: nothing yet; writing the specification.

STEP 2 - feasibility, cost and switch correctness
GOAL: confirm the mechanism is one run, no sweep, no ablation arm, and cheap at the frozen scale.
READ: frozen scale 24556 training items, 24 steps/epoch (batch ~1023), 3000 Stage-2 epochs = 72000 steps, Stage 3 150 epochs frozen.
OBSERVED: all constants are either measured once (delta, c from delta, alpha scale from epoch-0 distances, lambda from a 10-step gradient-norm ratio) or documented defaults (K=20 MST neighbourhood, delta measurement floor 0.05). Extra per-step work is ~2*|B| pair anchors x L prefix depths ~ 6k Poincare distances in d=64 plus one extra backward into the codebook, i.e. low single-digit percent of step time; the MST and delta precompute are CPU-only and sub-minute.
REASONING: no constant needs a sweep, the three switches (use_behavior, use_curvature, both on) are trivially separable, and only the both-on arm is trained.
OPEN: nothing; final answer below.

FINAL ANSWER - IDEA: DELTA-TREE-STRESS-RQ (Gromov-delta ultrametric curved stress on the RQ code embedding)
What it does: the negative curvature of the Poincare ball is initialised from the four-point Gromov delta of the training-transition behaviour metric (d_beh = -log((n_ij+1)/(sqrt(pop_i pop_j)+1))), delta_tilde = clip(delta_bar/D_b, 0.05, 0.5), c_delta = 1/delta_tilde^2, then made trainable as c = softplus(rho)+1e-6. Stage 2 adds lambda * L_str to the RQ-VAE loss, where L_str = (1/|P|) sum_l beta_l sum_P w_beh ( d_poincare_c(exp_0^c q_i^{:l}, exp_0^c q_j^{:l}) - alpha * t_tree )^2, on quantized prefix code embeddings q_i^{:l} = sum_{m<=l} C_m[k_i^m]. Targets come from the MST path-max ultrametric d_T of the sparse (K=20) behaviour graph, so the target is the tree structure the curved space represents well, not raw graph distance. Pairs are one near (MST child) and one far (t >= median) partner per anchor; w_beh = exp(-d_beh/D_b) normalised; beta_l = per-level residual-energy share measured at epoch 0; alpha = epoch-0 ratio sum w d_c / sum w t; lambda = median over the first ten steps of ||grad L_VAE||/||grad L_str||. All constants measured once then frozen - no sweep. Gradient lands on codebooks, encoder and rho, so codes and curvature both move.
Switches (exist, never trained off): use_behavior=False -> uniform pairs and t_tree = 0.5; use_curvature=False -> Euclidean in place of d_poincare_c; both on = the single run.
Leakage: counts, popularity, neighbours, MST, delta, c, alpha, lambda all from the Stage-2 training transitions only; no validation/test row, no Stage-3 feedback.
Judge: probe Spearman must beat the Euclidean RQ-VAE 0.0402 and top-10 behaviour-neighbour overlap 0.0124; then Stage-3 test_recall@10 > 0.065 with the explicit ~0.013 single-run noise caveat.
Cost: offline MST+delta sub-minute CPU, ~2 MB state; per step ~6000 Poincare distances (2*1023 anchors x L=3, d=encoder width) plus one extra backward into the codebook, low single-digit percent over 72000 steps (3000 epochs x 24 steps); Stage 3 frozen and untouched.
Distinct from earlier rounds: curvature is measured from the behaviour metric's own tree-likeness (Gromov delta), and the target is the subdominant ultrametric, applied at every prefix depth - not per-level prefix-transition curvature, not entropy-radial ranking, not successor-weighted Frechet codebook updates, not a metric swap on fixed codes.
Risks: delta_tilde near 0.5 makes the graph non-hyperbolic and the effect weak; probe may use token/prefix distance rather than code-embedding distance, so gains arrive only through prefix alignment; frozen alpha/lambda may be mis-scaled later.
Step records 1 and 2 above carry the design-space de-duplication and the feasibility/cost check. Answer printed in full in the response.
